subtitle: Final Fantasy warriors meet before the previous war

body: Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy is Square Enix's PSP fighting game, first released in Japan on 3 March 2011. Characters drawn from different Final Fantasy worlds take part in another cycle of the struggle between Cosmos and Chaos. The new campaign precedes the original Dissidia, then includes a revised version of that earlier story. Battles turn familiar heroes and villains into directly controlled fighters, while role-playing development and a world map connect the individual encounters. The release is both an expansion of the original idea and a new route through the crossover's continuing conflict.

Assist characters add another resource to the one-on-one battle, allowing support to change a dangerous situation or extend an opportunity. The player has to judge when that intervention is worth using rather than treating it as an automatic addition to every exchange. Familiar fighters and new arrivals bring different abilities into the arenas, encouraging the player to learn another style after mastering a favourite. Movement and attack remain tied to each character's particular strengths, while equipment and development give the wider campaign another layer beyond the immediate result of a duel.

Mitsunori Takahashi directed and Ichiro Hazama produced, with Takeharu Ishimoto composing the music. Development began in 2009 to refine the earlier systems, adjust their balance and introduce further features. A traditional world map gives the story another structure, while the inclusion of the previous campaign makes the release broader than a short prequel. International editions followed within March 2011. Reviews frequently placed it among the PSP's strongest games, recognising how the expanded cast, revised combat and extensive campaign gave the crossover idea more room to develop.
